Consider the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 1 \\ -1 \amp 3 \\ \end{bmatrix} $ whose characteristic equation is $$ \det(A-\lambda I) = \lambda^2 - 4\lambda + 4 = (\lambda-2)^2 =0. $$

There is a single eigenvalue $\lambda= 2$, and we find that $$ A - 2\lambda = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \amp 1 \\ -1 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$ Therefore, the eigenspace $E_2 = \nul(A-2I)$ is one-dimensional with a basis vector $\twovec11$.
